summary: Customer wants an optical measurement during yeast fermentation to follow growth and detect changes earlier. Biomass and metabolic signals are mentioned but not defined as separate targets. Broth becomes more optically dense during the run. They ask for help turning this into an initial feasibility study with reference measurements.

unknowns: Definition and range of the biomass target (e.g. OD, cell dry weight, viable count)
Definition of the metabolic signal (which metabolites or species, e.g. ethanol, glucose, CO2) and required range
Required accuracy, detection limit and response time
Reference method(s) available for calibration and validation
Installation point (at-line probe, bypass, in-line), distance and access
Matrix details: media composition, interferences, gas bubbles, fouling risk
Optical behaviour over the run: whether broth becomes opaque or remains turbid
Scale and type of fermenter, agitation, sampling frequency
Whether fluorescence or other modalities are acceptable/preferred
